record.title: An advertised missing sensor can block HID readiness
record.method: Matched baseline and single-node sensor-absence control; user/kernel stacks
record.observation: A HID registration worker waited through the unsupported legacy light-sensor path before signaling readiness. Omitting that unavailable sensor let the main thread and HID worker reach their event loops.
record.limits: This is an absence declaration, not a replacement sensor implementation. An event loop is not proof of input delivery.

exhibits.title: Baseline and sensor-absence control
rows: Service registration → ALS → legacy IIC wait
exhibits.interpretation: The worker signals readiness after registration returns. The paired captures connect the blocked sensor registration to the startup wait without claiming a working replacement sensor or live input.

excerpts.content:
The main thread waits in HID session initialization during application
startup. The same worker whose kernel stack reaches AppleISL29003 has this
user call chain: HID session thread, service-set traversal, service
registration, ALS state setup, HID service open, IOKit connection method,
Mach message. Exact library analysis shows the worker signals readiness
only after these registration calls return. Its kernel-side sensor call
is blocked on a shared legacy IIC controller queue. Other kernel threads
also wait on that controller; this does not identify a sensor register
failure or prove that this particular transfer reached hardware.

[…]

After the same 90-second observation window:

- SpringBoard has seven threads, compared with five in the baseline.
- Its main thread has left the HID readiness wait and reached
  GraphicsServices' event loop inside UIKit application run.
- The HID worker has passed registration/signaling and reached its own
  CoreFoundation run loop.
- The unsupported AppleISL service is absent; the buttons HID client still
  attaches. Other legacy IIC clients are not established as working.
- Both observed run-loop threads wait for Mach messages, which is expected
  at an idle snapshot. This does not prove input delivery or responsiveness.
- Captured display pixels remain XNU verbose text. No native graphical
  session, touchscreen or app interaction is demonstrated.
